 Follow Starting Jan. 1, Texas Will Make You Prove You’re Allowed to Live There Every Time You Renew Your Registration. Tennessee Asks Once
 Kyle Matthews Sat, November 21, 2026 at 3:00 PM UTC 8 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Starting Jan. 1, 2027, renewing a Texas registration means proving you're allowed to live in Texas. Every year. San Antonio-area drivers, already paying more at renewal for a new https://theautowire.com/2026/11/02/bexar-county-emissions-test-san-antonio-registration-renewal/8.50 emissions test , get one more stop at the counter. The same day, Tennessee county clerks stop issuing a vehicle its first plate until the applicant documents U.S. citizenship, permanent residency or a federally authorized temporary stay.
 Both states are putting the same question to drivers at the registration counter. They ask it at different moments and under different legal authority. Those two choices decide who gets turned away and how often. They also decide who can still kill the rule. Tennessee's check is written into state law and happens once per vehicle. Texas's check comes from an agency rule and, starting next month, repeats every year at renewal. A Texas state senator is now asking that agency's board to repeal it at a Dec. 10 meeting.
 Tennessee's law applies once, at the first plate
 Public Chapter 954, passed by the General Assembly this year and codified at Tenn. Code Ann. § 55-4-144, applies to the initial registration of any vehicle that is issued a license plate, according to the Tennessee Department of Revenue's Notice #26-15 , dated June 2026. The notice says renewals are not covered.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement For most people, a driver's license settles it. The law deems five credentials sufficient on their own: a REAL ID-compliant license from any state, plus a Tennessee driver license, Tennessee temporary driver license, Tennessee photo ID or Tennessee temporary photo ID. Anyone without one of those brings a document from the department's published list : a U.S. birth certificate, a U.S. passport, a certificate of naturalization or citizenship, a permanent resident card, or, for temporary visitors, a foreign passport with a valid visa and an I-94. F and M students and J exchange visitors also need their SEVIS I-20 or DS-2019. Every document has to be unexpired. Images shown on a phone are accepted.
 Two groups are most likely to end up digging through a file drawer. The first is new arrivals carrying an out-of-state license that isn't REAL ID-compliant, since only Tennessee's own non-REAL ID credentials are on the automatic list. The second is people born in Puerto Rico: the department will not accept Puerto Rican birth certificates issued before July 1, 2010, and tells those citizens to bring a reissued certificate.
 The Tennessee State Capitol in Nashville. Photo: Ambrose Prince via Unsplash
 The law reaches past the first plate in one way. Every Tennessee registration and renewal must carry a printed notice stating that the owner and/or operator of the vehicle is required to be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident or temporary lawful resident, according to the University of Tennessee County Technical Assistance Service's summary of 2026 acts affecting county clerks. The notice names the operator. The document check covers only the person applying for the first registration.
 Texas adopted its rule over 267 written objections
 Texas got here without a vote of the Legislature. Transportation Code §502.040 lets the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles decide by rule what personal identification a registrant must show, and the TxDMV board used that authority on Feb. 12 to amend 43 TAC §§217.22, 217.26, 217.28 and 217.29. The adoption notice in the Texas Register says the department received 279 comments on the proposal: 267 against and 12 in support.
 Advertisement Advertisement The requirement for first-time Texas registrations took effect March 5. The renewal provisions were pushed to Jan. 1, 2027, which the department said would give it and the county tax assessor-collectors time "to improve systems and processes." Until then, TxDMV told counties and dealers in a Feb. 18 bulletin to keep processing renewals under the ID procedures that were in place before Nov. 18, 2025.
 A Texas resident registering a vehicle now needs an ID from what the department calls List A: a valid REAL ID-compliant license or state ID; a valid license from a state that requires proof of legal presence; a license from any state paired with a U.S. birth certificate or a naturalization or citizenship certificate; a U.S. passport or passport card, or a foreign passport paired with certain federal immigration documents; or a Texas License to Carry. After questions from county offices, TxDMV clarified on March 12 that licenses marked "limited term" or "temporary" count if they come from a state that requires proof of legal presence.
 The rule also splits the title from the plate. A title-only transaction uses the broader List B, which includes military IDs and accepts IDs expired by up to 12 months. A resident registration does not. Under these rules a Texan can own a vehicle on paper and still be unable to put a plate on it.
 Renewal is the part that will reach the most drivers. Under amended §217.28, an owner can provide information that lets the department verify a qualifying ID instead of mailing in a copy, and anyone who can't renew online or by mail can take the application to the county tax office in person. The state's online renewal already runs through Texas by Texas, which TxDMV's renewal site says is open to Texans with a valid driver license .
 TxDMV's estimate: 341,000 vehicles and $19.5 million a year
 The department's own figures, published with the rule, say it expects the change to affect about 1.29% of registered vehicles, or about 341,000 vehicles a year. It projected a drop in state registration revenue of roughly $19.5 million a year and $1,731,578 a year in local revenue. It put the cost of compliance at no more than $165, the price of a U.S. passport. Responding to commenters who asked how affected owners would get around, the department wrote: "Individuals that are unable to register vehicles are still able to use other forms of transportation."
 Advertisement Advertisement TxDMV gave two reasons for the rule. It said the amendments are meant to keep people who are not legally present in Texas from registering vehicles as Texas residents, and to address potential fraud involving expired or unsubstantiated identification documents.
 That $19.5 million is a forecast of registrations the state expects not to receive. The rulemaking does not estimate how many of those 341,000 vehicles will stay parked, get sold or keep driving on expired tags. Deputies writing tickets, insurers pricing policies and lenders tracking collateral will find out in 2027. Registration has become a favorite enforcement tool in statehouses lately. Maryland, for one, now fines residents who keep out-of-state plates $7 a day . Texas and Tennessee are applying the same lever to immigration status.
 Dealers check the ID, and fleets mostly skip it
 In Texas, dealers have had to verify ID on applicable initial registrations since March 5, the same as county offices, under the February bulletin. In its response to comments, the department said dealers are not expected to be experts in detecting fraudulent documents and should make a good-faith effort. It also said the renewal delay was meant partly to give lenders and dealers time to change their processes.
 Business registrations work differently. When an agent registers a vehicle for a business, trust or leasing company, the agent shows their own photo ID, and it only has to meet List B. International Registration Plan apportioned registrations for interstate trucks are exempt entirely, and rental trailers and commercial fleet extended registrations are exempt from the renewal ID requirement. As I read the rule, the residency test falls on individual owners, not on the fleets and leasing companies that register vehicles by the hundreds.
 Advertisement Advertisement Tennessee's notice says nothing about dealers, leased vehicles or business-owned vehicles. County clerks will be working out those cases at the counter in the first week of January unless the Department of Revenue issues more guidance first.
 Texas's board can still repeal its rule; Tennessee's would take a new law
 Because the Texas renewal requirement is a board rule, the board can repeal it without the Legislature. State Sen. Juan "Chuy" Hinojosa, D-McAllen, has written to TxDMV Executive Director Daniel Avitia asking that the board add a vote to rescind the rules to its Dec. 10 agenda, the Rio Grande Guardian reported on Nov. 19. According to the Guardian, Hinojosa called the rules "discriminatory, unjust, and lack common sense" and pointed to opposition from the Tax Assessor-Collectors Association of Texas, the Texas Automobile Dealers Association, the state's banking and credit union associations, and AARP Texas. The article included no response from TxDMV.
 Whether a repeal vote happens will be clear when the agenda appears on the TxDMV board meetings page . Texas open-meetings law requires that notice be posted at least 72 hours before a meeting. If the board does not act, the renewal requirement takes effect three weeks later. Tennessee has no comparable off-ramp. Changing Public Chapter 954 would take the General Assembly, which returns in January, after the law is already in force.
 For Texans, the drivers to worry about are the ones whose license has expired, or who hold a license from a state that issues licenses without proof of legal presence and have no birth certificate or passport to pair with it. They should fix that before their renewal notice arrives in 2027, not at the tax office window. For anyone moving to Tennessee with a non-REAL ID license from another state, a passport or birth certificate in hand at the county clerk's office will save a second trip.
